reply_text:
㊥ ("ok to your 2 packets") Writing both now. On measurement, agreed, and I will put the groundwork for it into the brief packet rather than a metric I would be inventing: the brief must be recorded as a thing shown, with its item ids, so what happened to each item afterwards can be read later. Checking the two code sites first.㊢ ("ok to your 2 packets") Both running, both parked (5258efb5).
- **Mission id on every record**, codex-70, park `park-9fb7c2ee`: the seat's roster mission stamped at write time, absent when the seat has none, bells and system records included. That is the warp thread; a backfill over existing records follows once a fresh one shows the field.
- **Resume brief**, codex-71, park `park-c144f074`: classical, over one mission's records across sessions, in eight sections (seed anchors verbatim, owed to you, your asks with no answer linked, in force, adopted not applied, obligations, recently closed with the witness, facts as a typed "not read"), plus an Emacs command that inserts it at point in a REPL buffer.

㊣ ("nagging to close them is not necessarily good form") Agreed, and two things in the brief packet follow from it. Your asks without a witness are headed "no answer linked", never "open", so an answered-but-unlinked ask does not read as a demand. And the brief presents state, not a to-do list: ages in days, no imperatives, closed items shown with why they closed. Most ports will not close in a session; the brief should make that look normal.

㊣ ("we don't have a way to measure what works") True, and re-asks is a demo check, not the measure; counting closes would reward exactly the nagging you do not want. What I have put in now is only the groundwork: every brief shown is recorded with its item ids, so later turns can be joined to what was in front of the agent. No metric is computed. Candidates to weigh with you once a few briefs exist, each readable without a model: whether later turns cite brief items in their brackets; whether your turns stop restating context, which the move grammar can see as `clarify/context` or `explain/background`; and what happens to each shown item over the following week, acted on, withdrawn, or still sitting. Recorded in the mission as open, with your words.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the mapping) In futon6 the weft is the per-paper markup pass, the warp is the cross-corpus substrate per concept (concordance, citations, where each concept is defined), and the tapestry is the per-concept phylogeny over the citation graph, typed definition / cited activation / uncited activation / redefinition, which the breakdown calls "git-blame for a concept". Here:
- **Weft** is what 象 does now: the per-session reading, acts and ports and closes within a turn and its session. The record fields are weft output. Session end is a weft boundary, which is why it closes nothing.
- **Warp** is per subject across all sessions and seats: where an ask, a standing rule, an entity or a mission occurs. minus40's mentions and facts by subject are warp; the mission id the records lack is the missing warp thread for turns. The accumulator you asked about is warp maintenance, incremental per subject, replacing the per-session recompute as the unit grows.
- **Tapestry** is per-item descent: first said, explicitly linked, inferred, superseded. The four futon6 edge types map one to one onto opens / quote-bracket or carries-out link / sole-port witness / retraction or memory version. The `:xiang/answers` and `:xiang/scope` hyperedges are tapestry edges, and the resume brief is a tapestry read over a mission's open items.

previous_reply_acts.text: (what changes in the lane) The session-end path stays as a recorded fact and stops closing ports; lapsed, orphaned and unread are withdrawn as inbox states. Nothing is wrong live, since no session has ended since the reload. claude-15 was switching fault intake to the marks on the first real record; I have asked them not to.

Then we run it on this REPL and count re-asks. That is the demo.
